title: Pall Mall — passing the clubs (linear cut)
learning_goal: Linear-cut stand-in for the Street View walk: know the 1,151 steps and see the three clubs in a row.

narration.script: From Savile Row, Fogg walks to his club and counts. Five hundred and seventy-five steps with the right foot, five hundred and seventy-six with the left. One thousand one hundred and fifty-one. He never hurries. We are on Pall Mall now, walking west through clubland. It was one of the first streets in London lit by gas, in 1807. Watch the left side: the Athenaeum at 107, then the Travellers at 106. Then the palazzo with the tall windows — the Reform Club, 104 Pall Mall, by Charles Barry, opened 1841. Fogg made it 1,151 steps. We make it about a kilometre.

variants.clear: From Savile Row, Fogg walks to his club and counts his steps. One thousand one hundred and fifty-one steps. He never hurries. We are now on Pall Mall, walking west. This is clubland — a street of private clubs. It was one of the first streets in London with gas lamps, in 1807. Watch the left side: the Athenaeum at No. 107, then the Travellers at No. 106. Then the grand building with tall windows: the Reform Club, No. 104, by Charles Barry, opened 1841. Fogg counted 1,151 steps. We measure about one kilometre.
